data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The expert uses a holistic, non-decomposable process, while the panel uses a decomposed, additive process.","The expert's process is internal and opaque; the panel's is external and auditable."],"overturn_conditions":["If the expert's accuracy on complex cases is not statistically distinguishable from chance.","If the panel using a checklist also shows high accuracy on complex cases, suggesting the checklist captured the interactions."],"shared_structure":["Both involve making judgments under uncertainty.","Both can be evaluated against objectively verifiable outcomes."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["If expert intuition is a form of pattern matching on complex features, it will outperform on complex cases and underperform on simple ones.","Genuine reliability for the expert is not just being right, but being right on the complex subset where the checklist is confused."]},"claim":"Against the claim: a lone expert is more reliable because intuition efficiently integrates weak, interacting cues that a discrete checklist cannot encode.
